hypothesis.motivation:
The current 5-stage pipeline has two major microarchitectural bottlenecks:
1. Spurious load-use stalls: The hazard unit stalls the pipeline whenever the rd of a load in EX matches the raw rs1/rs2 bits of the instruction in IF/ID. However, many instructions (like LUI, AUIPC, JAL, etc.) do not read rs1/rs2, and many immediate instructions do not read rs2. Treating those raw bits as active register source operands causes frequent, unnecessary 1-cycle pipeline stalls, especially for consecutive loads with immediate offsets.
2. Multiplier combinational overhead: The ALU performs three independent 64-bit multiplications combinationally. This consumes a massive number of LUTs and limits Fmax due to the cascading delay in DSP blocks or carry chains.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
We propose two microarchitectural optimizations:
1. Add precise instruction decode information for rs1/rs2 active read signals (if_id_rs1_read and if_id_rs2_read) into the hazard unit. Only trigger load-use stalls if the dependent instruction actually reads the register.
2. Replace the three 64-bit multipliers in the ALU with a single shared 33-bit signed multiplier. By dynamically sign-extending or zero-extending the inputs based on the instruction type (signed, unsigned, or signed-unsigned), a single 33-bit signed multiplier can correctly resolve MUL, MULH, MULHU, and MULHSU, significantly improving Fmax and reducing LUT4 utilization.

title: One-Deep Store Retirement Slot With Direct Fast Path
motivation:
The baseline 5-stage core treats every dmem-not-ready cycle on a store as a
full pipeline freeze, even though a store's data and byte mask are already
known in MEM and no register result is needed by younger ALU/control
instructions. Under the tournament's random dmem stalls (~22%), this turns
store bus backpressure into lost execute bandwidth. A timing-local,
one-deep pending-store slot will decouple execute from these memory stalls,
significantly improving iterations per cycle (IPC) on store-heavy paths
without adding Fmax pressure.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a one-deep pending-store retirement slot that is used only on a legal,
aligned normal-RAM store when io_dmemReady is low. When io_dmemReady is high
and the slot is empty, stores drive the existing dmem outputs directly and
retire exactly as they do today. When io_dmemReady is low, the MEM stage
captures the store address, replicated write data, byte mask, and RVFI memory
metadata into the slot, retires that store once through MEM/WB, and lets
younger non-memory instructions continue while the slot drains. Younger
loads, younger stores, and all MMIO/marker/UART stores stall until the
pending store drains, preserving in-order memory visibility and exact
timing-marker behavior.

title: Two-bank registered lookahead instruction replay predictor with static branch/JAL predecode
motivation: The baseline RV32IM core always fetches sequentially and resolves all control flow in EX, incurring a 2-cycle flush penalty on every taken branch and jump. Additionally, the apples-to-apples evaluation environment drives ~22% random instruction-memory stalls, injecting significant bubble counts into the pipeline. Conventional branch predictors or target buffers often regress FPGA Fmax by putting instruction decode, target adders, tag comparisons, or return-address stacks directly on the timing-sensitive fetch next-PC path.

hypothesis.motivation: The baseline RV32IM core always fetches sequentially and resolves all control flow in EX, incurring a 2-cycle flush penalty on every taken branch and jump. Additionally, the apples-to-apples evaluation environment drives ~22% random instruction-memory stalls, injecting significant bubble counts into the pipeline. Conventional branch predictors or target buffers often regress FPGA Fmax by putting instruction decode, target adders, tag comparisons, or return-address stacks directly on the timing-sensitive fetch next-PC path.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
We propose a timing-clean, high-performance two-bank registered lookahead instruction replay predictor combined with stateless static branch/JAL predecode in the IF stage:
1. Replay Table: A 256-entry (128 per bank), two-bank direct-mapped replay table indexed by pc[8:2] and tagged by pc[31:9]. It caches successfully fetched instruction words and looks up the next-PC replay candidate one cycle ahead, completely removing table reads and tag comparisons from the same-cycle IF decision path.
2. iStall Hiding: When imem_ready drops, IF supplies the registered lookahead instruction and asserts fetch-ready, converting random iStall bubbles into zero-wait fetch cycles.
3. Static Predecode: Within IF, combinationally predecode JAL and backward conditional branches (negative displacement) from the fetched/replayed instruction, update the fetch next_pc early, and propagate the prediction.
4. EX Validation: EX verifies the prediction and asserts redirect only on a mismatch (mispredict), turning correct predictions into 0-cycle control transfers.
